Recognising grid events at a battery inverter

A battery energy storage system (BESS) connects to the grid through a power conversion system (PCS), an inverter. When the grid voltage dips, swells, jumps in phase, changes frequency or starts to wobble, the PCS must respond differently to each case. gridmon is a research prototype that looks at one second of three-phase voltage and says which of seven situations it was in — and it compares a transparent, standards-based rule set with a small machine-learning model on exactly the same physics features.

What the PCS must recognise — and why it matters

The seven classes (single label per 1 s record)
classwhat happens to the voltagetypical causePCS response it would drive (context only)
normalnothing beyond small everyday changes (the "hard negatives": small steps, ramps, harmonic changes)—none
sag_balall three phases drop together (below 0.9 pu)three-phase faultlow-voltage ride-through, positive-sequence reactive current
sag_unbalone or two phases drop more than the otherssingle/two-phase faultride-through with negative-sequence handling
swellall phases rise above 1.1 puload rejection, capacitor switchinghigh-voltage ride-through, absorb reactive power
phase_jumpthe voltage angle steps by several degrees, magnitude almost unchangedswitching, faults elsewhereride through — and must not be read as a frequency event
freq_eventthe frequency ramps or steps and stays away from 50 Hzgenerator or load tripfrequency response
oscillationslow (5–25 Hz) wobble of magnitude and anglepoorly damped control interactionsalarm / damping

Why the phase-jump row matters: in the 2016 Blue Cut Fire event in California, many inverters misread a phase jump as a frequency excursion and tripped [LIT]. The naive frequency rule on this site's Results page reproduces that failure mode; the rules and the small tree model here never confused the two on either test set.

How it works

System boundary and assumptions

Evidence tags: [STD] standard · [LIT] literature · [ASSUMED] engineering assumption · [SIM] this project's simulations · [EXP] experimentally validated (none in Stage 1).

  • Measurement: three line-to-line voltages at the PCS terminals (3-wire, so zero sequence is unobservable) [ASSUMED].
  • Records: 1 s at 5 kHz, 12-bit ADC over ±2 pu, from a triggered recorder; the event starts 0.2–0.4 s into the record and the first 0.15 s is pre-event [ASSUMED].
  • Dip and swell thresholds 0.90 / 1.10 pu follow IEC 61000-4-30 practice and IEEE 1159 categories [STD]; dip types follow Bollen's classification [LIT].
  • Strong grid: the PCS current does not change the voltage; no converter dynamics, no weak grids [ASSUMED].
  • All data are synthetic, from this project's physics-based generator (version 0.2.0): 5,600 training, 1,750 validation and 2 × 1,750 sealed test records [SIM].

Monitor-only

gridmon only listens. On a controller it receives copies of the voltages, keeps its own buffer and publishes a report; it never writes a control variable, a PWM register, a protection flag or a setpoint. Nothing from this project may be used for protection or control without separate validation on hardware and in the field (the validation ladder on the Firmware page).
